segments.title: Reading limits from a graph
segments.description:
Introduce x→a⁻ as approaching a from the left and x→a⁺ as approaching a from the right. Show the function h by its pieces and have students picture its graph from the description.
Students answer the six questions alone for four minutes, then compare with a partner.
Go over each one, using a sketch of h.
segments.teacherNotes: Answers: (a) 3; (b) 2; (c) does not exist; (d) h(0) = 1; (e) 2; (f) h(2) = 0. Students often answer (c) with 1 by reading the dot at x = 0. For (e), the value h(2) = 0 does not matter; near 2, h(x) = 2.

segments.title: Trace delete by hand
segments.description:
Students work alone on paper with the chain 4 → 8 → 1 → 6. They draw the chain after deleting 1, then after deleting 4 from the result.
Partners compare drawings and name the one reference that changed each time.
The teacher runs the code in the notes on the screen, and students check both drawings against the printed lists.
segments.teacherNotes:
Answers: after deleting 1: 4 → 8 → 6 (the 8 node now points to 6). After deleting 4: 8 → 6 (head moves to the 8 node). Watch for students who draw a gap instead of reconnecting the arrow. Students watch the run and do not type it.
`trace = LinkedList()`
`for value in (6, 1, 8, 4):`
`    trace.insert_front(value)`
`trace.delete(1)`
`print(trace.to_list())`
`trace.delete(4)`
`print(trace.to_list())`

segments.description: Short break. Leave the linked list code on the screen.

segments.title: Find and fix the bug in delete
segments.description:
Show a faulty `delete` for a linked list. Each student tests it on paper with the chain 5 → 2 → 8, deleting 5, and writes what goes wrong.
Students write a fix, then compare it with a partner’s.
Hear two fixes and test one live.
segments.teacherNotes:
Bug: the head is never checked, so deleting 5 leaves the chain unchanged and returns False; an empty list also raises AttributeError on node.next. Fix: add the empty check and head case from the earlier code. This replaces extra practice items.
`    def delete(self, value):`
`        node = self.head`
`        while node.next is not None:`
`            if node.next.value == value:`
`                node.next = node.next.next`
`                return True`
`            node = node.next`
`        return False`

segments.title: Find and fix the bug in the bracket checker
segments.description:
Show a faulty `is_balanced`. Each student tests it alone on paper with `((` and `())` and writes what goes wrong in each case.
Students write a fix, then compare it with a partner’s.
Hear two fixes and test one live.
segments.teacherNotes:
Bugs: `((` returns True because the final stack is never checked. `())` pops an empty stack and raises `IndexError`. Fix: test `is_empty()` before popping and return `stack.is_empty()`. Watch for students who fix only one of the two.
`def is_balanced_bad(text):`
`    pairs = {')': '(', ']': '[', '}': '{'}`
`    stack = Stack()`
`    for ch in text:`
`        if ch in '([{':`
`            stack.push(ch)`
`        elif ch in pairs:`
`            if stack.pop() != pairs[ch]:`
`                return False`
`    return True`

segments.teacherNotes: Hand out the papers face down and start together. Keep the board and screen clear of anything that could answer a question. Late arrivals take only the time left. Going over answers waits until the papers are collected.

segments.title: How the course runs and how it is graded
segments.description:
Walk through the course map: kinematics, Newton’s laws, work and energy, momentum, rotation, oscillations, using OpenStax University Physics Volume 1.
State the weekly rhythm of three lectures and one recitation.
Show the grading: weekly problem sets 20%, recitation group problems 10%, Midterm 1 20%, Midterm 2 20%, final exam 30%.
Students read the grading table, then write one question about the course and swap it with a neighbor to answer from the table.
segments.teacherNotes: Say that weekly problem sets are each student’s own work and recitation group problems are done in groups in the recitation. Exams are marked in points. Announce any exam policies yourself. Collect unanswered questions for the end of the session.

segments.title: SI units and chained conversion factors
segments.description:
Introduce the SI base units meter, kilogram and second, and derived units such as newton (kg·m/s²) and joule (N·m). Show prefixes from nano to giga.
Work 90 km/h to m/s as a chain of factors: 90 km/h × (1000 m / 1 km) × (1 h / 3600 s) = 25 m/s.
Students predict the next factor before each is written, and cancel the units aloud with a partner.
Revisit the opening question: 65 mi/h × 0.447 (m/s)/(mi/h) ≈ 29 m/s.
Mention the 1999 loss of NASA’s Mars Climate Orbiter, caused by a mismatch between pound-force and newton units.
segments.teacherNotes: Stress that units cancel like algebraic symbols. Common error: converting squared or cubed units with the linear factor. Use 1 mi = 1609 m for the exercises. Keep the Mars Climate Orbiter point to a sentence.

segments.title: Find and fix the mistake
segments.description:
Each student gets three flawed worked statements on the screen and writes the error and the corrected line for each.
Pairs compare their corrections.
Hear one pair on statement 3.
segments.teacherNotes: 1) 1 km² = 1000 m² is wrong: 1 km² = (1000 m)² = 10⁶ m². 2) 4.2 m × 1.37 = 5.754 m should be 5.8 m, two significant figures. 3) t = √(2hg) has dimensions L/T, not T; correct form is t = √(2h/g), valid for release from rest, constant g and negligible air resistance. These examples illustrate three checks: apply conversion factors to the correct power, report significant figures consistently, and check the dimensions of a formula.

segments.title: Adding and subtracting vectors
segments.description:
Show tip-to-tail addition on a drawing, then the component method: R = A + B gives Rₓ = Aₓ + Bₓ and R_y = A_y + B_y.
Work A = (4.0î + 2.0ĵ) m and B = (−1.0î + 5.0ĵ) m. The sum is (3.0î + 7.0ĵ) m, with magnitude 7.6 m at 66.8° above +x.
Students predict A − B before it is shown. It is (5.0î − 3.0ĵ) m, magnitude 5.8 m.
Show that subtraction means adding the negative, and that scalar multiplication scales every component.
segments.teacherNotes: Prediction answer: A − B = (4 − (−1), 2 − 5) = (5, −3). Common error: subtracting in the wrong order, which reverses the direction. Emphasize that components add, magnitudes do not.

segments.title: Integrate with initial conditions
segments.description:
Students work alone for five minutes on the problem on the screen.
They find v(t), x(t) and the position at t = 3.0 s.
They compare with a partner and the worked solution follows.
segments.teacherNotes: v = 4.0t − t², x = 2.0t² − t³/3. At t = 3.0 s: x = 9.0 m (v = 3.0 m/s). Check that a(t) = dv/dt returns 4.0 − 2.0t.

segments.title: Find and fix the mistake
segments.description:
Students read the flawed solution on the screen and write what is wrong and the corrected answer, working alone for five minutes.
Pairs compare and agree on a one-sentence rule that would prevent the error.
Two pairs report and the class checks the corrected answer.
segments.teacherNotes: Error: the deceleration was entered as +4.0 m/s² although velocity is positive. Correct a = −4.0, so Δx = +50 m. A negative distance behind the start is physically absurd, which is the check. Another common error: using these equations when a varies.

segments.description:
Show a classmate’s worked solution for five made-up study hours. It contains two errors.
Each student finds both errors alone and writes the corrected values.
Pairs compare, then the teacher hears the fixes and asks why each error is tempting.
segments.teacherNotes: Errors: the median was read from the unsorted list (14); sorted 2, 4, 6, 9, 14 gives median 6. The sd divided by n; correct is 88 ÷ 4 = 22, so s = √22 ≈ 4.69. The mean 7 is right. Students who finish early explain what a larger outlier would do to each result.

segments.title: Find and fix the mistakes
segments.description:
A classmate’s worked solution goes on the screen. It contains two errors, one in the outlier rule and one in the z-score.
Each student finds both errors alone and writes the corrected values.
Pairs compare, then the teacher hears the fixes and asks why each error is tempting.
segments.teacherNotes: Error 1: the student added 1.5, not 1.5 × IQR. Correct fences: 6.75 − 5.625 = 1.125 and 10.5 + 5.625 = 16.125. Only 30 is flagged. Error 2: subtraction reversed; z = (30 − 10.75) / 8.15 ≈ +2.36, so 30 hours is far above average. Mean and Q1, Q3 are right.
